data.title: bn-3glnv: signing wire — signer operations, signed receipts and bundles, intent.accept verification (protocol 3.8, IDL 1.16)

data.body:
[risk:high][CWE-345] Compare canonical contract bytes before treating an existing intent handle as identical. This branch skips any bundle entry whose IntentHandle already exists. The signed acceptance check at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:789-797 then selects the bundle entry only by that handle and compares only its record. A collision-capable ContentIdentifier, which the public builder seam permits, or a digest collision can therefore let a signature over body B accept distinct local body A under the same in_* identity. This violates RFC 0037 I6 and ADR-0013.

Failure modes: signed acceptance authorizes a byte-different local intent. The same missing exact comparison at signing.rs:693-706 lets a colliding inb_* retain one bundle while import applies another bundle's state changes.
Edge cases: existing proposed and accepted records, genesis and superseding records, identical-byte re-import, and collisions in intent and bundle handle classes.
Rollback: reject this range or disable bundle import and acceptance until exact comparisons land. A schema downgrade is not safe.
Monitoring: count and audit each equal-handle, different-canonical-bytes event as an identity collision. Do not log protected contract or key material.
Validation: inject a colliding ContentIdentifier. Prove import rejects before adoption or holding, and prove intent.accept cannot accept A from a signature over B. Keep identical-byte import idempotent.

data.reason: [risk:high] Bundle import skips canonical comparison for an existing in_* handle. A signature over one colliding contract body can authorize a different local body. See th-36jda8.

data.body: [resolved] Target 7b340d0 now compares each imported contract with exact held bytes before mutation at intent.rs:802-815, compares the accepted bundle entry with local canonical bytes at signing.rs:843-849, and rejects a held inb_ with different bytes at signing.rs:338-347. The collision tests cover all three paths.

data.reason: Exact-byte checks now close the reported import, acceptance, and held-bundle collision paths.

data.body:
[risk:high][CWE-345] Authenticate signer-lineage transitions instead of deciding authority from local familiarity. This loop stops before adding a predecessor already known without the exact link, so an importer that first learned active signer A can never later learn A to B from the successor bundle. The rotation at lines 624-632 is then skipped, A stays active, and its compromised signatures still pass CI acceptance. The inverse is unsafe: an unseen but separately pinned A enters B chain on B own assertion, which lets malicious pinned B mint, retire, or revoke A at lines 617-643. The bundle signature is checked only after these candidate facts are applied at lines 681-688. Local policy that pins A and B does not authorize either signer to forge the other signer transition.

Failure modes: normal rotation and loss recovery fail to retire a known predecessor, so a compromised old key remains trusted for intent acceptance. On first contact, one pinned signer can disable another unseen pinned signer.
Edge cases: predecessor first seen alone versus first seen inside the successor bundle; rotation and loss recovery links; later revocation; repeated bundles; record reordering; and a predecessor pinned locally but absent from the standing registry.
Rollback: do not adopt carried rotation or revocation facts, and do not enable the protocol 3.8 bundle acceptance path, until each lineage transition has proof acceptable to local policy. Keep old signers manually revoked during rollback.
Monitoring: count rejected carried links into known signers, carried links that introduce unseen pinned predecessors, and cases where both sides of a claimed rotation remain active. Do not log keys or bundle bodies.
Validation: first import a bundle from A, then import a B-signed bundle carrying A to B and an A revocation. Prove A becomes retired or revoked and B becomes active. Then let malicious B claim an unseen pinned A and prove A is not introduced, retired, or revoked. Repeat for loss recovery, replay, record reordering, and every atomic failure path.

[risk:medium][CWE-400] Preserve capacity to replace a compromised held key. A held-key compromised revocation may consume the full 4096-record bound at lines 1147-1160, but every later replacement mint uses the 4032-record ordinary bound here. If the log has at least 4031 records before revocation, revocation succeeds and all later mint attempts fail permanently. This contradicts the stated recovery path at lines 1161-1162 and leaves the deployment unable to sign. Reserve a replacement mint with the held-key revocation, or provide one atomic compromised-key replacement operation. Test boundary lengths 4030, 4031, 4032, and 4095, and assert that successful revocation always leaves a supported recovery path.

data.reason: High-risk signer-lineage verification is both incomplete and unsound: known predecessors cannot receive later rotation, while unseen pinned predecessors can be claimed by another signer. A medium recovery-capacity defect also remains.

data.body:
[risk:high][still-open][CWE-345] Multi-hop rotation adoption remains order-dependent at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:665-714. With A already active, local policy pinning A, B, and C, and a C-signed bundle carrying authentic links in order B-to-C then A-to-B, the first link rotates B. The second link sees B as non-active at lines 675-683 and drops A-to-B permanently. The bundle still verifies under active C, so A remains active. Reversing the two links retires A. The fixed-point claim at lines 601-604 is therefore false, and a compromised predecessor can remain trusted.

Failure modes: reordered multi-hop links leave an old compromised key active, so its bundle signatures and CI acceptance can still pass.
Edge cases: known A with unseen B and C; chains longer than two; reverse and mixed order; replay; a revocation after the skipped rotation; and quota boundaries.
Rollback: reject this range or disable carried signer-link adoption until dependency order is deterministic.
Monitoring: count authenticated links dropped because their successor is already rotated, and alert when a known predecessor remains active beside a reachable successor chain. Do not log keys or bodies.
Validation: prelearn A, import a C-signed bundle with B-to-C before A-to-B, then assert A is rotated or revoked and its signature fails CI acceptance. Permute every link order and require identical standing and audit facts.

[risk:high][CWE-347] Verify the acceptance signature and its chain, not only string equality inside a bundle. BundleRecord::parse accepts any nonempty signature text at intent.rs:570-584, BundleRecord::accepts only compares that text at intent.rs:601-606, and check_acceptance_chain verifies only the enclosing bundle signer at signing.rs:889-916. The tests confirm the accepted token is fabricated as repeated ab bytes at crates/continuumd/tests/daemon_signing.rs:412-414. RFC 0037 A1 requires the acceptance signature to cover the accepted intent, base or genesis marker, revise-intent capability, accepting principal, and timestamp. A3 also requires ordered chain-element verification under local policy. An allowed bundle signer can currently mint an accepted record for any principal and arbitrary signature string, and a privileged importer can promote it.

Failure modes: a bundle-signing key self-certifies governance acceptance or attributes acceptance to a principal who never signed it.
Edge cases: genesis versus revision, wrong base, wrong principal, wrong timestamp, malformed token, unknown or revoked acceptance signer, mixed-scope chains, and reordered or truncated chain elements.
Rollback: reject this range or keep bundle-backed intent.accept disabled until A1-A4 verification exists.
Monitoring: count AcceptanceChainInvalid by typed internal cause, especially malformed acceptance signatures and untrusted chain signers. Do not log signatures or protected contract bodies.
Validation: generate real acceptance keys and canonical A1 payloads. Mutate each covered field and each chain element independently. Require every mutation, unknown signer, revoked signer, reordering, and truncation to fail with AcceptanceChainInvalid. Remove the dummy-token positive fixtures.

[risk:high][CWE-345] Compare receipt bytes before reusing a receipt-node identity. This collision check at evidence.rs:1670-1673 compares only the staged commitment and profile. DaemonState::stage can overwrite byte-different content under one colliding commitment at state.rs:650-659. A later evidence.link with that same commitment therefore passes this check, signs the replacement bytes at evidence.rs:1706-1718, keeps the old append-only node at state.rs:938-947, and overwrites its signature at state.rs:701-708. evidence.get then returns an old node with a signature over different bytes. The added test uses Blake3 for staging, so it does not exercise this path.

Failure modes: a receipt node and publication record retain the first receipt while the returned signature authenticates replacement content under the same commitment.
Edge cases: collision-capable staging identifiers, same path and different bytes, different paths, retry after signer rotation, unsigned first link then signed replay, and signed first link then unsigned replay.
Rollback: reject this range or disable receipt-signature replacement until the node retains and compares exact signed receipt bytes.
Monitoring: count equal commitment and profile with different staged or published bytes as identity collisions. Do not log receipt bodies or keys.
Validation: stage two byte-different receipts through a colliding ContentIdentifier to one commitment. Link the first, overwrite staging, then relink. Require refusal before signing or publishing, preserve the original signature, and verify it only over the original bytes.

[risk:medium][still-open][CWE-400] The reserve fix protects states reached through these daemon operations, but the public installation path still admits the failing state. ReceiptSigner::new accepts any registry and signer at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/mod.rs:176-184, and SigningAuthority::install copies it without validating the record bound or replacement reserve at signing.rs:371-390. The new boundary test deliberately installs 4094 and 4095-record registries, then confirms held-key revocation succeeds while replacement returns QuotaExhausted at daemon_signing.rs:2941-3007. Thus a restored or externally built registry can still revoke its held key successfully and become permanently unable to mint a replacement. Validate the installed registry and held-key standing against the reserve invariant, or make compromised revocation and replacement atomic.

data.reason: BLOCK: three risk:high integrity failures remain. Multi-hop signer-link adoption is order-dependent and can leave a compromised predecessor active; bundle-backed intent acceptance compares but never cryptographically verifies the RFC 0037 A1/A3 acceptance signature chain; receipt-node reuse can overwrite an old node's signature with a signature over byte-different staged content under a colliding commitment. The installed-registry recovery boundary also remains risk:medium. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains required.

data.body: [resolved] Target bec8be93 refuses byte-different staging collisions in DaemonState::stage, retains each receipt node’s first exact bytes and first signature, and compares those bytes before any relink signs or publishes. The collision and replay tests cover the original failure path.

data.reason: Fixed at bec8be93: exact receipt bytes and first signature are retained and collision-checked before signing.

data.body: [resolved] Target bec8be93 adds the intent-acceptance signed kind and verifies every RFC 0037 A1 field, chain position, signer identity, active standing, and local-policy permission. The bundle record’s acceptance signature must equal the verified chain end. Mutation tests cover the original forged-token path.

data.reason: Fixed at bec8be93: RFC 0037 A1-A4 acceptance signatures and ordered chains are verified under local policy.

data.body: [resolved] Target bec8be93 requires every carried transition to be attested by each key it concerns, refuses conflicting rotation topology, and applies disjoint rotation chains from their first key in deterministic key order. The permutation and prelearned-predecessor tests cover the original authority and order defects.

data.reason: Fixed at bec8be93: key-attested disjoint rotation chains are applied in deterministic dependency order.

data.body: [risk:medium][still-open][CWE-400] Target bec8be93 validates only that an active installed key has one revocation slot at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/mod.rs:206-218. It still accepts 4094- and 4095-record registries. A compromise revocation then consumes one record, while replacement mint requires two slots at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:1248-1253. The boundary test at crates/continuumd/tests/daemon_signing.rs:3682-3718 explicitly accepts those installations, and the earlier test confirms replacement is QuotaExhausted. The deployment can still lose signing permanently after a successful emergency revocation.

[risk:high][CWE-835] Reject malformed rotation graphs before traversing them. links_are_attested mutates successor and predecessors while computing well_formed at signing.rs:1074-1084. It then follows successors without a visited set at signing.rs:1088-1094, even when well_formed is false. Three validly attested links A-to-B, B-to-C, and C-to-B make B have two predecessors. The predicate becomes false, but the maps retain A-to-B-to-C-to-B. A remains a first key, so the loop never terminates. intent.import_bundle reaches this check for any self-authenticated outer bundle at intent.rs:858-865, before local-policy verification. A privileged unscoped caller can therefore hang synchronous daemon dispatch with untrusted bundle bytes. The current test covers only a pure cycle, which has no first key and terminates.

Failure modes: one import never returns and can pin the daemon worker or process, denying all work behind it.
Edge cases: a tail entering a two-node or longer cycle, duplicate predecessors, link permutations, a pure cycle, a shared successor without a cycle, maximum link count, and replay.
Rollback: disable bundle import, or reject conflicting topology before any traversal. Do not enable bundle-backed acceptance through this path.
Monitoring: count malformed link graphs before traversal. Alert on import CPU or dispatch deadlines. Do not log keys or bundle bodies.
Validation: build signed links A-to-B, B-to-C, and C-to-B. Require immediate MalformedRequest with no state change. Permute the links and extend both tail and cycle. Assert each edge is visited at most once.

data.reason: BLOCK: [risk:high][CWE-835] links_are_attested can loop forever on a validly attested tail entering a cycle; see th-d3x20n. [risk:medium][CWE-400] installed registries can exhaust replacement capacity after emergency revocation; see th-36mges. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains required.

data.body: [resolved] Target 44536e4e requires three free records for every active installed key at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/mod.rs:209-220. RECOVERY_RECORDS accounts for the held-key revocation, replacement mint, and replacement revocation at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:137-145. Replacement mint reserves its own revocation at signing.rs:1280-1286. The boundary tests accept 4093 records and reject 4094 through 4096.

data.reason: Target 44536e4e restores the full three-record recovery reserve.

data.body: [resolved] Target 44536e4e checks every in-degree and out-degree defect at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:1097-1109 before traversal. It then marks each source and bounds traversal by the edge count at signing.rs:1115-1129. The import gate remains before mutation at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/intent.rs:858-871. Tail-cycle, pure-cycle, shared-successor, duplicate-edge, and permutation cases cover the reported failure.

data.reason: Target 44536e4e rejects malformed topology before bounded traversal.

Whole persisted range reviewed at 44536e4e. The recovery-reserve and malformed-topology findings are resolved. No security blocker remains. This static LGTM does not replace the separate risk:critical human-approval gate.
